title: Project Evidence Record gap recovery via public job-description signals
objective: Test whether current public job descriptions can expose under-documented but potentially real professional experience without allowing market language to become an unsupported resume claim.
hypothesis: Cross-referencing Project Evidence Records against recurring job-requirement signals will identify high-value UNKNOWN or PARTIAL evidence fields that can be resolved by targeted human interrogation and supporting evidence.
null_hypothesis: The cross-reference produces mostly generic questions, creates no material new verified career evidence, or encourages unsupported relabeling of prior work.
inputs: Current resume evidence already encoded in seven Project Evidence Records
Current public job-description sample across AI/technical program management, quality systems, research operations, and clinical/quality leadership
method: Compare PER evidence coverage with recurring market requirement signals
Mark absent or under-specified fields UNKNOWN or PARTIAL rather than negative
Require human attestation and/or evidence before promoting a response into a durable career claim
Reuse newly verified evidence across future role-specific applications
guardrails: UNKNOWN may remain UNKNOWN without penalty
success_criteria: At least one material previously undocumented claim is recovered and evidenced without fabrication
Each promoted claim retains source provenance and confidence state
Question burden is reduced by reusing answers across multiple applications
Role-specific resumes can distinguish supported, partial, and unresolved requirements
falsifiers: Questions are too generic to recover distinct evidence
User cannot distinguish recollection from documented fact
Market terminology systematically induces inflated claims
Recovered claims do not improve application evidence coverage
The same evidence cannot be reused reliably across role families
next_action: Human completes the Career Evidence Interrogation Frontier; responses are then classified as SOURCE_SUPPORTED, HUMAN_ATTESTED, INFERRED, or UNVERIFIED and reconciled into PERs.
